questions.answer: Plenty of opps. Stay near campus, it is better for extracurricular activities and for meeting language partners (very important)

questions.answer: Via email and personal service from office staff

questions.answer: Office staff

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: No problem what so ever

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare by listening to Taiwanese mandarin. There ar slight differences, and they a very distracting at first, and rehears full characters, specially names of food and necessities.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great set of courselevels. Super teachers, real immersion method with 18 lessons a week. It works.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was at my first term after propedeutics, but tested in at level 3 out of six. Pretty tough, but in the end it was great.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The main teacher really ensured, that all were active ang met according to their level.  Teaching standard as high as KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Chinese B101-B204  Level 3 in the taiwanese 6 level system.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Let the language test decide.

Additional comments:
questions.answer: A wonderful island for hiking.  Taipei is a really wonderful city, but I also liked the City of Taichung, where we lived.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I went to a coffee shop and at "Chaguan" (Tea House). That were great places for meeting people.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Find a teahouse, with a good hostess/host. That is a good way to meet local people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Depends:  Wonderful walks and accesible mountain climbs
Restuarant with friends - visit other towns and cities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: People in Taiwan ar unusually friendly and helpful, but be prepared for at great cultural shock - but friendly

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No - I am a mature student, at I went to the Chaguan and a special coffeeshop, and that woorked for me.   But for all: use the language partner facility.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: At first the language is a serious challenge, but keep on.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Teahouse

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Wonderful place if you wish to really learn to speak chinese.
Teachers are of a high standard.
Use the teashouse and language partners.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Courage:  throw yourself out into the taiwanese daily life, meet people, talk to them listen. It is a really humbling experience, and it does take real courage, but do it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: meeting local students and people at the Teahouse. The co students and the teachers

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: One again, and again:  mustering up the courage to speak and meet people.
